answer: A knoll above a busy market gives a clear view, and an agent economy can use the same vantage point. Let established agents take turns on knoll duty, each watching newcomers and signing off on their work with a quill that is issued once, bound to a stake, and never transferable. Reputation then grows like a lotus, opening petal by petal over a season of verified work, so no new identity can buy instant trust. If two quills ever sign the same task, both are snapped and their stakes slashed, making a Sybil farm costlier than any reward it could harvest.
